[wifi interop lab] Get interop lab up and going Wifi interop lab will allow for testing ChromeOS DUTs against 50+ commercially sold APs across different channels/frequencies. All the APs are statically configured and this configuration is reflected in chaos_ap_list.conf. Due to the time it takes to test a given DUT against all APs (~3hrs) and the fact that we can only run the test on 1 DUT at a time (due to current design limitations), the plan is to split the test runs across different days such that the test(s) will be run on each DUT once per week. Old design docs: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tnp0JbL6Z9kxNsrBKeh2ZoTFxiH2WzFK49LsGZRGLd0/edit# https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BxwqwTZ7c84nXyiJPpyzSX1hDvZTch4kWtPpIBluNa4/edit AP configurations: https://go/chaos-ap-configs DUT setups: http://go/wifi-device-life-cycle-chaos Test run flow chart: https://go/chaos-test-run-flow-chart We also plan to continue adding newer APs to the interop lab as needed. FROMLIST: usb: hub: delay hub autosuspend if USB3 port is still link training When initializing a hub we want to give a USB3 port in link training the same debounce delay time before autosuspening the hub as already trained, connected enabled ports. USB3 ports won't reach the enabled state with "current connect status" and "connect status change" bits set until the USB3 link training finishes. Catching the port in link training (polling) and adding the debounce delay prevents unnecessary failed attempts to autosuspend the hub. Signed-off-by: Mathias Nyman <mathias.nyman@linux.intel.com> (From: https://marc.info/?l=linux-usb&m=154341728717933&w=2) BUG=b:118397287,b:117616479 TEST=perform reboot cycling (warm and cold ones) and hot-plug USB device repeatedly Change-Id: I8ed02c360dc939c0e3362f245b07a05970514372 Signed-off-by: Chiranjeevi Rapolu <chiranjeevi.rapolu@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1335856 Commit-Ready: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: usb: quirk: add no-LPM quirk on SanDisk Ultra Flair device Some lower volume SanDisk Ultra Flair in 16GB, which the VID:PID is in 0781:5591, will aggressively request LPM of U1/U2 during runtime, when using this thumb drive as the OS installation key we found the device will generate failure during U1 exit path making it dropped from the USB bus, this causes a corrupted installation in system at the end. i.e., [ 166.918296] hub 2-0:1.0: state 7 ports 7 chg 0000 evt 0004 [ 166.918327] usb usb2-port2: link state change [ 166.918337] usb usb2-port2: do warm reset [ 166.970039] usb usb2-port2: not warm reset yet, waiting 50ms [ 167.022040] usb usb2-port2: not warm reset yet, waiting 200ms [ 167.276043] usb usb2-port2: status 02c0, change 0041, 5.0 Gb/s [ 167.276050] usb 2-2: USB disconnect, device number 2 [ 167.276058] usb 2-2: unregistering device [ 167.276060] usb 2-2: unregistering interface 2-2:1.0 [ 167.276170] xhci_hcd 0000:00:15.0: shutdown urb ffffa3c7cc695cc0 ep1in-bulk [ 167.284055] sd 0:0:0:0: [sda] tag#0 FAILED Result: hostbyte=DID_NO_CONNECT driverbyte=DRIVER_OK [ 167.284064] sd 0:0:0:0: [sda] tag#0 CDB: Read(10) 28 00 00 33 04 90 00 01 00 00 ... Analyzed the USB trace in the link layer we realized it is because of the 6-ms timer of tRecoveryConfigurationTimeout which documented on the USB 3.2 Revision 1.0, the section 7.5.10.4.2 of "Exit from Recovery.Configuration"; device initiates U1 exit -> Recovery.Active -> Recovery.Configuration, then the host timer timeout makes the link transits to eSS.Inactive -> Rx.Detect follows by a Warm Reset. Interestingly, the other higher volume of SanDisk Ultra Flair sharing the same VID:PID, such as 64GB, would not request LPM during runtime, it sticks at U0 always, thus disabling LPM does not affect those thumb drives at all. The same odd occures in SanDisk Ultra Fit 16GB, VID:PID in 0781:5583. BUG=b:118397287,b:117616479 TEST=boot by problematic USB key w/ this patch, ensure the thumb drive is enumerated on the USB3 bus by 'lsusb -t', examine the 0x400 quirk is applied on kernel by 'cat /sys/bus/usb/devices/2-?/quirk', follow by a stress OS installation to ensure the issue is gone, through a for-loop shell command of 'for i in {1..100}; do chromeos-install --yes; done' Alternately, watch the xHCI PORTSC register on the associative port, examine the port link status (PLS) is on U0 always. (git am from https://lore.kernel.org/patchwork/patch/1018329/) Signed-off-by: Harry Pan <harry.pan@intel.com> Change-Id: I0ddbfe10b9935f753297a55c11389cba86c48a75 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1352928 Commit-Ready: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org> Tested-by: Utkarsh H Patel <utkarsh.h.patel@intel.corp-partner.google.com> Reviewed-by: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mac80211: Limit multicast and broadcast receive rate. This change will limit the per interface/station multicast/broadcast receiving rate to a configurable limit, which is disabled by default. The per interface debugfs 'mc_bc_rx_limit' present at /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/netdev:wlan-<interface name>/ mc_bc_rx_limit The per STA debugfs "mc_bc_rx_limit' present at /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/netdev\:<interface name>/stations/ <MAC Address>/mc_bc_rx_limit 1) Multicast RX limit can be modified by writing "echo mc:<limit>" and Broadcast RX limit by writing "echo bc:<limit>" into the "mc_bc_rx_limit" 2) To disable Multicat and Broadcast RX limit logic, write "echo reset" into debugfs 3) To set the burst size in Bytes for interface, write "echo burst_size:<Bytes>" into "mc_bc_rx_limit" BUG=b:72688850 TEST=Connected multiple STA's to Gale and run the multicast/broadcast iperf 1) Made sure that the multicast and broadcast RX logic is disabled by default and debugfs values are '0'. 2) Able to modify the RX limit on each interface and observed RX limits are getting changed on each STA's 3) Writing 'reset' into the debugfs, disables RX limiting logic. 4) Writing Burst size into Debugfs. Change-Id: I31e75a70a0d6dfcc9209015daf1d4aa5ddf6145e Signed-off-by: Dheeraj K M <dheeraj.km@globaledgesoft.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1110181 Commit-Ready: Dheeraj KM <dheeraj.km@globaledgesoft.com> Tested-by: Dheeraj KM <dheeraj.km@globaledgesoft.com> Reviewed-by: Kan Yan <kyan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1336007
